newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: PanAmSat satellite launch rescheduled.
newsitem.headline: PanAmSat satellite launch rescheduled.

text.p: The PANAMSAT-6 (PAS -6) satellite planned for launch from French Guiana aboard Western Europe's 96th Ariane on May 13 has been delayed until late summer, officials said on Thursday.

"Based on recommendations by Space Systems/Loral, the PAS-6 spacecraft supplier, PanAmSat has postponed the launch to determine what, if any changes should be made to the power system on the spacecraft," Greenwich, Connecticut-based PanAmSat said in a statement.
The decision to reschedule the PAS-6 launch is connected to an ongoing investigation by Loral into the cause of power decrease on a similar FS-1300 model satellite.
PanAmSat currently operates four satellites providing video and data communications services to customers world-wide.
PAS-6 had been set for launch aboard Western Europe's 96th Ariane rocket from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
